verses.text: Then Jesus began to speak to them using stories. He said, "A man planted a vineyard. He put a wall around it and dug a pit for a winepress. He also built a watchtower. Then he rented the vineyard out to some farmers and went away on a journey.
At harvest time he sent a servant to the farmers to collect his share of the fruit from the vineyard.
But they grabbed the servant and beat him. Then they sent him away with nothing.
Then the man sent another servant to them. They hit this one on the head and treated him shamefully.
He sent still another servant, and they killed him. He sent many others. They beat some of them, and they killed others.
The man had one more person to send. It was his son, whom he loved. Last of all, he sent his son to them. He said, 'They will respect my son.'
But the farmers said to each other, 'This is the one who will receive everything one day. Come, let us kill him, and everything will be ours.'
So they took him and killed him. Then they threw him out of the vineyard.
"What will the owner of the vineyard do then? He will come and kill those farmers. Then he will give the vineyard to other people.
Have you never read this Scripture? 'The stone the builders rejected has become the most important stone of all.
The Lord has done this, and it is wonderful to see.'"
Then the leaders looked for a way to arrest Jesus, because they knew he had told the story against them. But they were afraid of the crowd. So they left him and went away.
Later they sent some Pharisees and some of Herod's supporters to Jesus. They wanted to trap him with his own words.

They came to him and said, "Teacher, we know that you are honest. You do not let others tell you what to do, and you treat everyone the same. You teach the way of God truthfully. Is it right to pay taxes to Caesar or not?
Should we pay them or not?" But Jesus knew they were being hypocrites. "Why are you trying to trap me?" he asked. "Bring me a silver coin. Let me look at it."
They brought the coin. He asked them, "Whose picture is this? And whose words?" "Caesar's," they replied.
Then Jesus said to them, "Give to Caesar what belongs to Caesar, and give to God what belongs to God." And they were amazed at him.
Then some Sadducees came to Jesus. They do not believe that people rise from the dead. They asked him a question.
"Teacher," they said, "Moses wrote for us that if a man dies and leaves a wife but no children, his brother must marry the widow. Then he must have children for the brother who died.
There were seven brothers. The first one married and died without having any children.
The second one married the widow, but he also died and left no children. It was the same with the third one.
In fact, none of the seven left any children. Last of all, the woman died too.
When the dead rise, whose wife will she be? All seven of them were married to her."
Jesus replied, "You are wrong, because you do not know the Scriptures or the power of God.
When the dead rise, they will not marry, and they will not be given in marriage. They will be like the angels in heaven.
Now, about the dead rising, have you not read in the book of Moses the story about the bush? God said to Moses, 'I am the God of Abraham, the God of Isaac and the God of Jacob.'
He is not the God of the dead, but of the living. You are badly mistaken!"
One of the teachers of the law came and heard them arguing. He saw that Jesus had given them a good answer. So he asked him, "Which is the most important of all the commands?"
Jesus answered, "The most important one is this: 'Listen, Israel. The Lord our God is the one and only Lord.
Love the Lord your God with all your heart, with all your soul, with all your mind and with all your strength.' This is the first command.
The second is this: 'Love your neighbour as you love yourself.' No other command is greater than these."
"Well said, Teacher," the man replied. "You are right in saying that God is one, and that there is no other god but him.

To love him with all your heart, with all your understanding, with all your soul and with all your strength is very important. So is loving your neighbour as you love yourself. These things are more important than all burnt offerings and sacrifices."
Jesus saw that the man had answered wisely. He said to him, "You are not far from the kingdom of God." From then on, no one dared to ask Jesus any more questions.
While Jesus was teaching in the temple, he asked, "Why do the teachers of the law say that the Christ is the son of David?
David himself, speaking by the Holy Spirit, said, 'The Lord said to my Lord, "Sit at my right side until I put your enemies under your feet."'
David himself calls him 'Lord'. So how can he be David's son?" The large crowd listened to him with joy.
As he taught, Jesus said, "Watch out for the teachers of the law. They like to walk around in long robes. They like to be greeted with respect in the marketplaces.
They love to have the most important seats in the synagogues and the best places at dinners.
They take away the houses of widows, and they make long prayers to show off. These men will be punished more than others."
Jesus sat down across from the place where people put their offerings. He watched the crowd putting their money into the offering boxes. Many rich people put in large amounts.
But a poor widow came and put in two very small copper coins. Together they were worth almost nothing.
Jesus called his followers to him. He said, "I tell you for certain, this poor widow has put more into the offering box than all the others.
They all gave out of their riches. But she gave out of her poverty. She put in everything she had to live on."
